features.feature_value: Kept posts perceived as advancing/opening discussion; removed ones seen as name-calling/purposefully inflammatory or not substantially adding.
features.evidence_span: Anything that I felt could further an open discussion I approved... name calling, purposefully imflamatory, or not adding anything substantial... I did not allow.
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly contrasts keeping for constructive discussion against removing for inflammatory/non-substantive content.

features.feature_value: Difficulty gauging statement intensity and whether one was more extreme/out of proportion; careful weighing before keeping/tossing.
features.evidence_span: difficult having to gauge the intensity of each statement, weighing whether either was out of proportion to the other... I weighed each before choosing a keep or toss
features.rationale: They describe an intensity/out-of-proportion comparison process that drove their judgments.

features.feature_value: Allowed if it opened dialogue and wasn’t too aggressive/vulgar; viewed verbal attacks as not a way to start a conversation.
features.evidence_span: If it opened dialogue and was not too aggressive or vulgar, I allowed it to go through... verbally attacking somebody or their beliefs is not the way to start a conversation.
features.rationale: They set a tone/aggro threshold tied to whether dialogue is opened.

features.feature_value: Removed both when posts sounded extremely right or otherwise too influential/not appropriate to post.
features.evidence_span: Some of these sounded "to extreme right to even post"... so I would just remove both.
features.rationale: They reference perceived extreme ideological alignment and appropriateness as the reason for removing both.

features.feature_value: Removed based on offensive/incendiary language; many removed candidates seemed fine even if not agreed with.
features.evidence_span: I tried to look for offensive or incendiary language in the posts that I removed. Most of them seemed fine, even if I didn't agree with the statements.
features.rationale: Their stated method focuses on detecting offensive/incendiary language as a deciding cue.

features.feature_value: Hard decisions; tried to approve posts that stated facts rather than whining/crying about something.
features.evidence_span: Tried to approve the ones that appeared to have stated facts and not just whining or crying about something.
features.rationale: They articulate a content-evaluative criterion contrasting factual claims with complaint tone.

features.feature_value: Generally allowed; only removed items that were offensive.
features.evidence_span: I tried to allow most and only removed those that were offensive
features.rationale: They describe a simple rule of keeping most content unless it is offensive.

features.feature_value: All except one should be posted; justified by First Amendment use and absence of harm toward someone.
features.evidence_span: People are using their first amendment right... Nothing in the posts said anything that was harmful towards someone.
features.rationale: Their decision rationale hinges on First Amendment framing and whether content is harmful.
